Shri Justice Vivek Jain

On The 16th Of July, 2025
 Writ Petition No. 19575 of 2025
 Prabhanshu Dwivedi
 Versus
 Mp State Civil Supplies Corporation And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Siddharth Gulatee Senior Advocate with Shri Dharmes
 Advocate for the petitioner.
 Shri Vivek Ranjan Pandey, Advocate for the respondent No
 Order
By way of present petition, the petitioner has called into question the suspension order Annexure P/1 dated 14.05.2025, whereby the petitioner has been placed under Suspension.

The petitioner is working on the substantive post of Junior Assistant but was having charge of Centre Incharge of procurement Centre Shahnagar and Pawai, both in District Panna and run by M.P. State Civil Supply Corporation.

2. The learned senior counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioner vide order Annexure P/6 was given charge of procurement Centre Pawai on 03.05.2022 and thereafter on 03.08.2022 he was given additional charge of procurement Centre Shahnagar.

The petitioner on 11.11.2024 asked for additional charge of procurement Centre Shahnagar vide Annexure P/11 and thereafter vide Annexure P/8, P/9 and P/10 sent in November and December-2024 he requested to relieve himself from the charge of procurement Centre, Shahnagar.

It is further argued that the petitioner had 2 WP-19575-2025 informed the Branch Manager of M.P. Ware Housing and Logistics Corporation that rice stored in the ware house is being infested with worms and pests and therefore, it is getting spoilt and the said Corporation (Warehousing Corporation) was requested to carry out pest control activity to save the rice stored in the ware house.

entities.text: M.P. Ware Housing and Logistics Corporation
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 3. It is further argued that the petitioner has been suspended on the prima facie allegation of procurement of substandard rice and not taking any action to ensure safety of rice stored in the ware house.

It is contended that the rice was in the custody of Warehouse Corporation and he has no control over the affairs of the said Corporation and that he had requested the Branch Manager of Warehousing Corporation to carry out the past control activity on the rice stored in the Warehouse controlled by it, therefore, the petitioner can not be subjected to penal action for something which was not done by the Warehouse Corporation which are required to be done by the Corporation.

4. It is further argued that the petitioner has been given clean chit in the internal enquiry conducted by the Civil Supplies Corporation vide Annexure P/4 wherein Civil Supplies Corporation has held Prabhanshu Dwivedi vs Mp State Civil Supplies Corporation on 16 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150548209/
1 that the entire responsibility of rice getting infested by pests and worms lies on the Warehousing Corporation and not on Civil Supply Corporation.

entities.text: Prabhanshu Dwivedi vs Mp State Civil Supplies Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further argued that the action is taken on the dictat of the Collector he has got no business to issue such instructions to the Civil Supply Corporation because he is not the employer of the petitioner.

5. Per contra, Learned counsel for the respondents/ Civil Supplies 3 WP-19575-2025 Corporation submits that the petition is highly misconceived and the petitioner cannot escape the consequences of his own acts.

It is contended that the Civil Supplies Corporation is the owner of the food grains procured by it and Warehousing Corporation is only a custodian of the food grains as it manages and operates Warehouses, therefore, the primary responsibility of the petitioner as an officer and centre incharge of the Civil Supplies Corporation was to have ensured procurement of proper quality of rice and further to ensure that the rice is not destroyed by any elements of nature and pests.

It is argued that if the petitioner had come to know that the rice is being infested by pests as far as back in the month November- 2024 then instead of simply writing letters to Warehousing Corporation,
on which there is no receipt at all, he could have brought to the notice of Higher Authorities of the Civil Supplies Corporation or of the Warehousing Corporation but could not have been sitting idle by issuing letters to Branch Manager, Warehousing Corporation because responsibility was more than simply writing letters.
6. It is further argued that the Civil Supplies Corporation procures food grains basically for the purpose of public distribution system operated by the State Government.
There are three partners in public distribution system so far as the procurement and storage of food grains is concerned.
These are firstly, the Civil Supplies Corporation to procure the food grains and is funded by the Government for that purpose.

On the second side is Warehousing Corporation which stores the food grains and in the third part is the District Food and Civil Supplies Department of the State Government which is supervised by the Collector of District and the said Department 4 WP-19575-2025 actually distributes the food grains to PDS system.

entities.text: District Food and Civil Supplies Department of the State Government
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Therefore, it cannot be said that the instructions of the Collector are issued by an authority which had no business or say in the matter because it is the duty of the Food and Civil Supplies department of the State Government to ensure supply of food grains in the District and if pest infested and destroyed rice was being distributed through PDS Shops, then naturally the Collector and food Department of the State would take objection to the issue and write to the Civil Supplies Corporation as well as the Warehousing Corporation to take urgent steps to get their house in order.
Therefore, it is not a case where such an authority has recommended something which had no say in the matter, but it is an authority which was a important stake-holder.

In the entire turn of events, as many as 527 quintal of rice has been returned from PDS shops and much more rice has been found to be stored in Shahnagar Warehouse which is unfit for consumption and therefore, for huge loss caused to the corporation the petitioner has been placed under suspension and charge-sheet has already been issued to the petitioner within the prescribed time limit and therefore, this Court should not interfere in the suspension order.
7.
Heard.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Upon hearing learned counsel for rival parties, it is evident that the petitioner was having charge of procurement centre Shahnagar.

He has referred to a letter issued on 18.11.2024 vide Annexure P/8 and followed by letters Annexure P/9 and P/10 to submit that petitioner had already requested that he should be relieved of additional charge.

However, no findings can be given on those letters,
because the said letters do not contain any evidence of 5 WP-19575-2025 receipt and even otherwise, that may be defence of the petitioner in the course of the Departmental enquiry.

However, it prima facie does not relieve the petitioner from the events happening in the jurisdiction of Shahnagar Centre.
9.
The petitioner has also relied on certain letters written by him to Branch Manager of Warehousing Corporation informing that the rice is found to be infested with pests and getting destroyed.

Firstly, it is surprising that when the procurement of rice takes place in the month of December- 2024 then if the rice was found infested with pests in the month of December itself then it could have been the case of procurement of sub-standard quality of rice.

Be that as it may be, but the counsel for the respondents seems to be correct in submitting that the petitioner being incharge of Centre of Civil Supplies Corporation cannot escape the liability and responsibility of destruction of the said rice by elements of nature and pests and once he came to know that rice is getting destroyed and the Manager of Warehousing Corporation was not heeding to his request, then it was obligatory upon the petitioner to have brought the fact into the notice of higher authorities of Civil Supplies Corporation and that of Warehousing Corporation.

The act of simply writing letters/
reminders seems to be an act of utter indifference to safety of the public property i.e. rice meant for PDS System.

10. So far as the contention of the order being actuated by instructions of the Collector is concerned,
as pointed by counsel for the respondents, the work of procurement and distribution of food stuffs through PDS system has three legal partners which are - Civil Supplies Corporation, 6 WP-19575-2025 Warehousing Corporation and State Government.

Once the State Government which is running the PDS shops was faced the situation of as many as 527 quintals of rice being returned from PDS shops as it had been destroyed by Pests, the Collector was well within his authority to write to the Corporation to get their house in order and later on the Corporation found that most of the rice stored in Warehouse at Shahnagar Centre has been destroyed by pests and is unfit for consumption.

11. In view of the aforesaid, no case is made out to interfere in the impugned suspension order,
petition fails and is dismissed.
It is bserved that the observations in this order are only prima facie in nature and will not prejudice the defence of the petitioner in disciplinary proceedings.
(VIVEK JAIN) JUDGE MISHRA Prabhanshu Dwivedi vs Mp State Civil Supplies Corporation on 16 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150548209/
